# aeneid-076 drafter notes (X.362–438)

42 units. Title `Pallantis virtus. Halaesus et Lausus`; part "Pallas Rallies the Arcadians (X.362–438)".
¶ units: 362 only (Greenough's single paragraph start in this part). make_units.py prints no warnings.

## Misprints (rule 5b; t kept as printed, l/i corrected)
- **10.371 `Opemque` for `spemque`.** Treated as a clear misprint, not a doubtful reading, for two reasons:
  (1) metre: `ops, ŏpis` has a short first syllable (L&S), so `Opemque meam` cannot open a hexameter, whereas
  `spēmque mĕ|ām patri|ae quae | nunc subit | aemula | laudi` scans; this is also why the scanner gives UNRESOLVED;
  (2) the capital O mid-sentence — Greenough capitalises only after a stop or for a proper name, and Ops the goddess
  makes no sense with `meam`. The Latin Library has `spemque`. l/i read "my hope, which now rises to rival my
  father's glory"; the note of unit 369–372 opens with the rule-5b sentence. If the reviewer prefers to keep
  `opem` as a doubtful reading, the sense would be "my strength/might, which now rises to rival…", and only that
  phrase and the note's opening need changing. **Scansion consequence:** the scan-fix for 371 should scan the line as
  if `spemque`: spem que me | am pa tri | ae quae | nunc su bit | ae mu la | lau di (DDSDD + final foot).
- No other misprint found: speech marks at 369/378 and 421/423 sit correctly (no mark joined to the next word);
  checked for lowercase after a stop and odd letters.

## Doubtful readings / variants noted in n
- 10.366 `quis` (= quibus) vs LL `aquis` — noted (relative "for whom" vs "rough with water"). `quis` = quibus noted
  again at 435.
- 10.363 `impulerat` vs `intulerat` — mentioned in one clause as near-identical sense.
- 10.378 `petemus` vs `petamus` — noted briefly (future vs deliberative subjunctive).
- 10.390 agris/arvis, 10.401 direxerat/derexerat, 10.412 conligit/colligit — mentioned only in passing as no change.
- 10.378 `Troiam`: taken as probably the Trojan camp ("new Troy"), with the old city noted as possible; hedged.
- 10.426 `perterrita` taken with `agmina` (predicative with `sinit`), the usual construction.
- 10.428 `pugnae nodumque moramque`: rendered as the knot where the fight was tied up and held back.

## Attributions written from memory, not checked against a text
- Ajax's appeal at the ships as model for Pallas's speech, Iliad 15.733–741.
- Agenor on Achilles' mortality, Iliad 21.568–570.
- Fire simile parallels, Iliad 11.155–157 and 20.490–492.
- Merops of Percote keeping his sons from war, Iliad 2.831–834 and 11.329–332.
- Ennius, Annals, `semianimesque micant oculi` (fragment on a severed head; quoted by ancient commentators).
- Anchemolus story (Rhoetus king of the Marsi, stepmother — named Casperia in Servius, not given in the note —
  flight to Daunus): from memory of Servius, attributed in n only to "the old commentators".
- Halaesus as Agamemnon's follower (VII.723f.); Lausus second in beauty to Turnus (VII.649f.); Abas in the
  Etruscan catalogue (X.170ff.); Pallas's later prayer to Hercules refused (X.460ff.); Turnus stripping Pallas's belt.
- `imperdita` as Virgil's coinage; `addensent` from `addenseo` (rare form).

## Decisions
- Advisory: none. Battle killing (incl. 413–416 skull/brains, 395–396 severed hand) is ordinary battle narrative,
  consistent with 067–075. 389 Anchemolus "dared to defile his stepmother's bed" is a passing mention of incest
  (consensual seduction in the source story), not sexual violence; no advisory.
- 377–378 kept as one unit (2 lines) rather than splitting at `fugae:`, so the closing question stays with its image.
- 400 cut twice (`traicit.` / `Ilo;`) so the Ilus aside stands on its own.
- No new house renderings; new-renderings.md says "None." sc not written.
